Parcels

Australia Post opens parcel hub on air force base

By Alex PackAugust 3, 20261 Min Read
Share LinkedIn Twitter Facebook Email
Credit: Australia Post
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:12
Instaread

Australia Post has opened its first parcel hub on the Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) base in Darwin, giving defense personnel from 21 nations access to mail and parcel services during Exercise Pitch Black, the RAAF’s biennial international air combat exercise.

Operating throughout the exercise, the dedicated parcel hub gives Australian and international personnel deployed to Darwin access to postal services, including the movement of urgent freight and the return of equipment. Free 24/7 parcel lockers have also been installed on base, giving personnel greater flexibility when sending and receiving parcels throughout the exercise.

Australia Post general manager Mitch Buxton said the initiative reflects the company’s ongoing focus on adapting services to meet customers how and where they need them.

“Australia Post has a longstanding partnership with defense, and this first-of-its-kind portable parcel hub shows how we are innovating to meet the changing needs of our customers,” Buxton stated. “The hub is designed to operate in complex environments, and this exercise in Darwin will give us valuable insight into how we can strengthen our emergency response during natural disasters, severe weather events and other major disruptions.”

In related news, ACCC clears Australia Post stamp price increase to A$1.85
